title: Appeal of RE Choon Soon Lee vs. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; the SJC held that Korean Capital Presbytery and its January 8, 2001 Special Judicial Commission were not the proper court of original jurisdiction, and reversed their actions in receiving and adjudicating charges against RE Choon Soon Lee. The underlying charges were not decided on the merits.
first_summary: Korean Capital Presbytery suspended RE Choon Soon Lee from the sacraments. The SJC sustained his appeal and reversed, holding that the Session, not Presbytery or its commission, should have had original jurisdiction over the charges. No merits decision was made, and one commissioner dissented.
summary: Korean Capital Presbytery approved a three-year suspension from the sacraments after its special judicial commission found RE Choon Soon Lee guilty of contumacy and making a false statement on a civil-court document. On appeal, the SJC sustained and reversed. Because Lee was a communicant member, the Session—not Presbytery or its commission—was the court of original jurisdiction; the commission's adjudication therefore violated constitutional standards. The SJC did not decide the underlying charges, and one commissioner dissented.

evidence_notes.dispute: KCP suspended RE Lee after its special judicial commission adjudicated charges against him (lines 18–32); the issue asks whether Presbytery or its January 8, 2001 Special Judicial Commission was the proper court to assume original jurisdiction (lines 40–42).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC answered no and reversed Presbytery/commission actions (lines 44–57); reason: the Session is the court of original jurisdiction for communicant members, so neither KCP nor its commission could adjudicate charges against Lee (lines 50–57).
